name: Customer segmentation
summary: Split customers into groups with different needs, value and behaviour (demographic, needs-based, behavioural, B2B firmographics), size and value each segment, then choose targets and positioning (STP).
opening_line: I'd segment customers by the dimension that most changes their needs or value, size each segment and its profitability, and then decide which ones to target.
when_to_use: When averages hide differences (profitability by customer, pricing by segment)
when_not_to_use: When the customer base is homogeneous and the question is operational

buckets.name: Evaluate
questions: Which segments are biggest, most profitable and most winnable?

industry_adaptations.note: Segment by wealth tier (mass, mass affluent, affluent, HNW, UHNW) with very different profitability.
Needs and price tier (mass vs prestige), channel preference.

common_mistakes: Segmenting on a dimension that doesn't change behaviour
Not sizing or valuing the segments
